name: Gold intraday seasonality around London AM/PM fixes and Asian-session drift
source_url: https://research.cbs.dk/en/studentProjects/gold-price-dynamics-around-the-clock/ (Donati & Jung, CBS student thesis); World Gold Council 2024 intraday note (URL not retrieved) [uncertain]; Caminschi & Heaney (2014) and Hauptfleisch, Putnins & Lucey (2016) for fix microstructure
author_year: Donati & Jung (CBS master's thesis, year not confirmed) [uncertain]; Caminschi & Heaney (2014); Hauptfleisch, Putnins & Lucey (2016); World Gold Council (2024)
instrument: XAUUSD (Maven MT5 symbol availability and name not verified [uncertain])
timeframe: Intraday; sources use 20-minute mid-price (WGC 2024) and 24-hour session analysis (thesis); hourly per research request [uncertain]
entry_rule: No replicable entry rule found in the sources. Thesis describes a hat-shaped intraday pattern: gold rises during Asian/eastern hours and falls for the rest of the day. An anecdotal 'buy at PM fix, sell in the morning' claim (FXStreet, citing Ed Steer) is commentary, not research [uncertain]
trades_per_year: Not applicable without a defined rule [uncertain]
overnight_weekend: The thesis hat-shaped pattern spans 24 hours and therefore includes overnight (Asian session) moves; any rule built on it would hold overnight. Tradability with Maven swap and FundedNext overnight rules not verified [uncertain]
signal_window_definition: Not defined in readable sources. LBMA gold fixes are set by auction at 10:30 and 15:00 London time (general knowledge, not verified in this session) [uncertain]. DST handling: not extracted [uncertain]. Thesis uses a 24-hour clock
sample_period: Thesis sample period not extracted [uncertain]; WGC 2024 note covers January to October 2024 (20-minute mid-price data)
out_of_sample: None found. No 2023 to 2025 out-of-sample test of gold London fix hourly returns was located in the search results
cost_assumption: Thesis backtests reported before costs; no post-cost results found [uncertain]
reported_metrics: Thesis: Sharpe ratio up to 1.61 in pre-cost backtests (per search snippet) [uncertain]. WGC 2024: gold's return in 2024 was driven mostly by Asian trading hours (no numeric magnitude extracted). Caminschi & Heaney (2014): significant returns for informed traders in the 4 minutes after fix start; no significant effect after fix publication
third_party_replication: None found for the hourly gold seasonality claim. Fix microstructure has independent academic work (Caminschi & Heaney 2014; Hauptfleisch, Putnins & Lucey 2016), but these do not test an hourly trading rule
evidence_grade: Student thesis (weakest tier for a trading claim); industry research note (WGC, descriptive); older peer-reviewed fix microstructure papers (not a trading rule); anecdotal commentary
decay_status: Thesis states the London-fix drop occurred mainly in years of alleged manipulation, which implies the effect may have changed after reforms. Not quantified [uncertain]
regime_split: Thesis splits by alleged manipulation years versus other years (qualitative). Numeric split not extracted [uncertain]
data_source_requirement: Hourly or 1-minute XAUUSD history from Maven MT5 with time-zone-correct timestamps; LBMA fix times are public. Maven gold history depth and spread not verified [uncertain]
min_lot_fit_5k10k: Stop not defined. Illustration only: on many brokers 0.01 lot XAUUSD equals 1 oz, so a 20 USD stop risks about 20 USD = 0.4% of USD 5,000 or 0.2% of USD 10,000. Contract size must be confirmed on Maven [uncertain]
fn_rule_fit: Not verified against FundedNext rules [uncertain]. Gold is highly sensitive to scheduled US releases (for example 15:00 London, 10:00 ET overlaps) and the +/-5 minute news rule would apply to those releases [uncertain]
bot_policy_compliance: A pure time-of-day rule is implementable as an EA with no messaging link. FundedNext bot policy not verified in this session [uncertain]
event_overlap: LBMA PM fix (15:00 London, general knowledge [uncertain]) overlaps with US 10:00 ET releases such as Conference Board and ISM; London AM fix overlaps with the European open
overlap_with_existing: High with the existing Donchian XAU 1H module (same instrument, overlapping session); a gold seasonality rule would be correlated with it [uncertain]
rejected_catalog_hit: Not checked. Run: python -m intraday.elenenler --kontrol gold (in the main session) [uncertain]
base_rate_check: Not computed. Gold has a positive drift and the thesis compares hours without a stated base rate [uncertain]
pitfall_risk: High. (1) Hour-of-day bins: about 24 hourly tests produce false positives without correction; (2) pre-cost backtests only; (3) sample not out-of-sample; (4) thesis-level evidence with unknown sample dates; (5) regime change after reforms
